_comment: Boundaries asserted on every build by foundation-platform's archcheck, which this
repository reuses rather than reimplements: `go run
A package absent from internalEdges may import no internal package.
An edge not declared here fails the build.
cmd/ packages are the driving adapters. They are the only packages permitted to start a
goroutine and the only place dependencies are constructed, which is why cmd is absent
from noGoroutineSegments while domain and app are listed.

_comment_db: internal/db is the only package permitted to bind a transaction's isolation scope, per
TDD-organization-control-001. It has no internal edges on purpose: a package that could
reach a repository or a service could resolve a scope from something other than the
authenticated context, which is the substitution the RLS layer is a second line of
defence against. binding_test.go asserts the SQL side by walking the repository.

github.com/jackc/pgx.reason: no package in this repository names the driver. foundation-platform's db package is the single place it is named, and every signature here carries db.Tx instead, so replacing the driver is one module's change rather than this repository's

database/sql.reason: the pgx pool in foundation-platform is the only connection source. a second one would open connections outside the transaction manager, and outbox.Append would no longer be atomic with the domain mutation it accompanies

net/http.reason: this service reaches no other domain over HTTP. ADR-ORG-001 5.4 gives it neither the Keycloak administration credential nor a network route to the kernel, and that prohibition is structural rather than procedural: an HTTP client here would be the first step toward the projection path the Identity Control Service owns. The composition root will be excepted when it serves, and nothing else
